cox_subgroup_forest() Tutorial

Julian Silan

2026-08-19

This tutorial walks through cox_subgroup_forest() end to end using survival::lung, a built-in dataset of advanced lung cancer patients. It covers data preparation, forest plot for each covariate and a combined one, categorical vs. continuous covariates, custom reference levels, level exclusion, multiple endpoints, and the main styling arguments.

Source the function first (adjust the path to wherever forestplot_subgroup_function.R lives relative to this .Rmd file):

source("/Users/julian/Desktop/VHIO/R code/Forestplot/Subgroup/forestplot_subgroup_function.R")
library(survival)
library(dplyr)

1 Prepare the data

survival::lung needs a little massaging before it’s ready for Cox modelling: status is coded 1/2 (censored/dead) rather than 0/1, sex is an unlabelled numeric code, and ph.ecog is stored as numeric even though it is really an ordered categorical performance-status score. We also add a synthetic treatment arm and a synthetic PFS endpoint so the tutorial can demonstrate multivariable models and multi-endpoint plots.

set.seed(42)

lung2 <- survival::lung %>%
  mutate(
    event_os  = status - 1,                       # 1 = death, 0 = censored
    time_os   = time,
    sex       = factor(sex, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Male", "Female")),
    ph.ecog   = factor(ph.ecog),                   # 0-3 performance status
    treatment = sample(c("Arm A", "Arm B"), n(), replace = TRUE),
    time_pfs  = pmin(time_os, time_os * runif(n(), 0.4, 0.9)),
    event_pfs = ifelse(time_pfs < time_os, 1, event_os)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ph.ecog), !is.na(sex), !is.na(age))

#glimpse(lung2)

time_pfs / event_pfs here are a simulated PFS endpoint (PFS event always occurs no later than OS) purely so the tutorial has two endpoints to work with — survival::lung does not contain real PFS data.

2 The simplest use

The simplest possible call: one categorical covariate, one endpoint, univariable model.

res_sex <- cox_subgroup_forest(
  data = lung2,
  covariates = c("sex"),
  labels = c("Sex"),
  treatment = "treatment",
  time = c("time_os"),
  event = c("event_os"),
  endpoint_labels = c("Overall Survival"),
  time_unit = "days",
  palette = c("#0F084B")
)

res_sex$results_table

  time = c("time_os"),
  event = c("event_os"),
  endpoint_labels = c("Overall Survival"),
  time_unit = "days",

)

3.1 Specify x-axis

res_x <- cox_subgroup_forest(
  data = lung2,
  covariates = c("sex", "ph.ecog"),
  labels     = c("Sex", "ECOG PS"),
  treatment = "treatment",
  time = c("time_os"),
  event = c("event_os"),
  endpoint_labels = c("Overall Survival"),
  time_unit = "days",
  palette = c("#0F084B"),
  xlim = c(0.25, 4),
  ticks_at = c(0.5, 1, 2)
)

res_x$combined_plots

4 Excluding a level

ph.ecog == "3" has only a handful of patients in lung. exclude_levels drops it by setting those values to NA, which then falls out through the existing complete-case filtering used inside each model:

res_excl <- cox_subgroup_forest(
  data = lung2,
  covariates = c("sex", "ph.ecog"),
  labels = c("Sex", "ECOG PS"),
  treatment = "treatment",
  time = c("time_os"),
  event = c("event_os"),
  endpoint_labels = c("Overall Survival"),
  time_unit = "days",
  palette = c("#0F084B"),
  exclude_levels = list(ph.ecog = "3"),
  xlim = c(0.25, 4),
  ticks_at = c(0.5, 1, 2),
  length_plot = 60,
  #weights = "weights_ATE", # optional if PS used
  ci_pch = 15, 
  ci_lty = 1,
  ci_lwd = 3, 
  ci_Theight = 0.4, 
  sizes = 1,
  row_height = 1.4,
  covariate_label_row = TRUE
)

res_excl$combined_plots

For a multivariable model this exclusion drops the affected patients from the entire model (since multivariable fitting requires complete cases across every covariate simultaneously) — see the next section.

5 Multiple endpoints (OS and PFS) with colour coding

Pass time and event as vectors, paired by position, along with matching endpoint_labels. With more than one endpoint the plot automatically colour-codes the confidence intervals per endpoint and adds a legend below the figure.

res_two_ep <- cox_subgroup_forest(
  data = lung2,
  covariates = c("sex", "ph.ecog"),
  labels = c("Sex", "ECOG PS"),
  treatment = "treatment",
  time = c("time_os", "time_pfs"),
  event = c("event_os", "event_pfs"),
  endpoint_labels = c("Overall Survival", "Progression-free Survival"),
  time_unit = "days",
  palette = c("#0F084B", "red"),
  #exclude_levels = list(ph.ecog = "3"),
  xlim = c(0.25, 4),
  ticks_at = c(0.5, 1, 2),
  length_plot = 60,
  #weights = "weights_ATE", # optional if PS used
  ci_pch = 15, 
  ci_lty = 1,
  ci_lwd = 3, 
  ci_Theight = 0.4, 
  sizes = 1,
  row_height = 1.4
)

res_two_ep$combined_plots

6 Styling the plot

A few of the most commonly adjusted arguments:

res_styled <- cox_subgroup_forest(
  data = lung2,
  covariates = c("sex", "ph.ecog"),
  labels = c("Sex", "ECOG PS"),
  treatment = "treatment",
  time = c("time_os", "time_pfs"),
  event = c("event_os", "event_pfs"),
  endpoint_labels = c("Overall Survival", "Progression-free Survival"),
  time_unit = "days",
  palette = c("#0F084B", "red"),
  #exclude_levels = list(ph.ecog = "3"),
  xlim = c(0.25, 4),
  ticks_at = c(0.5, 1, 2),
  #weights = "weights_ATE", # optional if PS used
  ci_pch = 15, 
  ci_lty = 1,
  ci_lwd = 3, 
  ci_Theight = 0.4, 
  sizes = 1,
  row_height = 1.4,
  covariate_label_row = TRUE
)


res_styled$combined_plots

  • row_height — multiplier applied to every body row’s height (1.4 = 40% taller); useful when labels wrap or the figure feels cramped.
  • covariate_label_row = TRUE inserts a dedicated bold row with just the covariate name above its levels, instead of bolding the first level row in place.
  • xlim / ticks_at let you fix the axis range and tick marks manually instead of relying on the automatic (CI-range-based) defaults — handy for keeping several related figures on the same scale.
